items.label: Choose joystick
items.note: Plug in a radio in joystick mode. If more than one is plugged in, this is how you pick which one flies.

items.label: Recognised as
items.note: Plug in a radio in joystick mode or a gamepad and move a stick. Until then the keyboard flies.

items.label: Calibrate sticks
items.note: Centre, full range, then one named move per stick. Saved after you check it.

items.label: Check sticks
items.note: Your saved mapping, live, without calibrating again. Move a stick and watch it: if it goes the wrong way, one key reverses that channel, and if the wrong stick moves on screen, one key puts them on the other hands. Nothing is kept until you save.

items.label: Stick mode
items.note: Which stick is throttle and which is yaw, the way your radio is set up. Mode 2 is throttle on the left, which is what this page has always been. Mode 1 puts throttle on the right and pitch on the left. This flies the THUMB STICKS and the KEYBOARD, which have no mode of their own. A radio already applies its own mode before this page sees a stick, so for a radio this only names the sticks drawn on screen.

items.label: How the sticks fly, every multirotor
Rates
items.note: Yours for every multirotor: another kind of aircraft keeps its own, and starts on its stock until you change them. How far the sticks go, and how sharply. Yours, not the tune's. A radio in Acro flies this curve; keyboard flight is Angle. Changing them mid run leaves the quad where it is and the clock running.
items.value: Actual, 670 roll and pitch, 670 yaw deg/s

items.label: Keys and buttons
items.note: Move the flight keys: reset, unstick, flip, launch, chute, flaps, gear, smoke, the view and stepping out.

items.label: Mouse flight
items.note: The scroll wheel is the throttle and holds where you leave it; the mouse is the right stick, sideways rolls and forward and back pitches. The left and right buttons yaw, the middle button or Z centres the stick, and every keyboard key still works. In flight the pointer is captured: Escape frees it and pauses, a click takes it back. On, it flies instead of a connected radio.

items.label: p_pitch
items.note: How hard the controller corrects the error it can see right now. More holds the line harder and shakes more in propwash.

items.label: i_pitch
items.note: How hard it corrects error that has been there a while. This is what holds an angle against wind and against a heavy battery.

items.label: d_pitch
items.note: Damping ceiling. Resists fast movement, which is what stops P ringing. Configurator apps call this D max.

items.label: f_pitch
items.note: Feedforward. Pushes on stick MOVEMENT, before any error has appeared, so the quad starts turning with your thumb rather than after it.

items.label: Iterm relax
items.note: Screen group. Values still travel as CLI.

items.label: iterm_rotation
items.note: Rotates accumulated I with the craft as it yaws, so I earned on roll does not end up fighting pitch after a spin.

items.label: iterm_relax
items.note: Which axes stop accumulating I while the sticks are moving. Without it, a fast flick banks up I that then springs back when you stop: the bounce at the end of a roll.

items.label: iterm_relax_type
items.note: Whether relax watches the gyro or the setpoint. Setpoint is the modern default and reacts to what you asked for rather than to what happened.

items.label: iterm_relax_cutoff
items.note: How quick a stick movement counts as moving. Lower leaves relax on for longer and is calmer; higher lets I build sooner and holds better.

items.label: iterm_windup
items.note: The motor saturation point past which I stops growing, so a quad pinned at full throttle does not bank up correction it can never deliver.

items.label: iterm_limit
items.note: A hard ceiling on how much I is allowed to contribute at all.

Stock sits at 100; the stiff preset that used to ship here sat at 185, which is about the size of step that feedback was asking for.

items.label: Tracking, P and I
items.note: How hard the quad chases the rate the stick asks for. Low is lazy and smooth, high snaps onto the setpoint and holds it.

spec.label: Tracking, P and I
spec.note: How hard the quad chases the rate the stick asks for. Low is lazy and smooth, high snaps onto the setpoint and holds it.

items.label: Drift and wobble, I
items.note: The slow-error term on its own. Too low drifts off attitude in wind-up moves; too high winds during a long throw and dumps it as a twitch when the stick centres. On this plant the twitch arrives well before the drift.

spec.label: Drift and wobble, I
spec.note: The slow-error term on its own. Too low drifts off attitude in wind-up moves; too high winds during a long throw and dumps it as a twitch when the stick centres. On this plant the twitch arrives well before the drift.

items.label: Damping, D
items.note: Resists rotation, smooths stops, calms propwash. On a real quad D is paid for in motor heat and gyro noise; this model’s gyro is clean, so damping is nearly free and the stiff tunes run it high.

spec.label: Damping, D
spec.note: Resists rotation, smooths stops, calms propwash. On a real quad D is paid for in motor heat and gyro noise; this model’s gyro is clean, so damping is nearly free and the stiff tunes run it high.

items.label: Dynamic damping, D max
items.note: How much extra D arrives during fast moves and stops, on top of the base D. Zero holds D constant.

spec.label: Dynamic damping, D max
spec.note: How much extra D arrives during fast moves and stops, on top of the base D. Zero holds D constant.

items.label: Stick response, FF
items.note: Feedforward pushes on stick movement itself, before any error exists. High is immediate; too high overshoots the start of every move. Zero flies on P and D alone.

spec.label: Stick response, FF
spec.note: Feedforward pushes on stick movement itself, before any error exists. High is immediate; too high overshoots the start of every move. Zero flies on P and D alone.

items.label: Pitch tracking
items.note: Pitch P and I relative to roll. A quad is longer than it is wide, so pitch usually carries a few percent more.

spec.label: Pitch tracking
spec.note: Pitch P and I relative to roll. A quad is longer than it is wide, so pitch usually carries a few percent more.

items.label: Language
items.note: The words on every screen. Changing it reloads the page; nothing else changes.

items.label: Your name
items.note: The name this computer flies under. Two to twenty four letters, numbers, spaces, dots, underscores or hyphens.

items.label: Pilot key
items.note: On the board your name belongs to a key kept in this browser, made the first time you post. Export copies it, to carry your name to another browser or to keep it safe.

items.label: Import pilot key
items.note: Paste a key exported from another browser. Times you post from here then count as that pilot, and the key that was here is gone.

items.label: Flight time
items.note: Time in the air, counted from your first takeoff. Pauses, menus and replays do not count.

items.label: Controller
items.note: Which device flies, its calibration, dead zone and expo, the stick mode, and the keys and buttons.

items.label: Show sticks
items.note: Your two sticks over the flight, low in the middle, whatever you fly with. Flying by keyboard or mouse shows them anyway.

items.label: Compare sticks
items.note: Opens a control recording, one of your own flights or the flight lab's pilot, and plays its sticks as a ring on your sticks from the moment you are in the air. Choose it again to put it away. It is kept until the page closes.

items.label: Radio link
items.note: No radio: every frame arrives, exactly on time. Feedforward and RC smoothing read that cadence, so this is sharper than any real link.

items.label: Stick latency
items.note: Low hands the flight controller each stick reading in the frame it was read instead of the next one, so a move reaches the picture about 5 ms sooner on average. Recordings and replays are unchanged, since they hold what reached the flight controller.

items.label: Tune, PIDs and the firmware
items.note: Those belong to the machine, not to you, so they are one room over under Quad. Camera angle and flight mode are there too.

items.label: Graphics
items.note: A 2021-era PC or a strong laptop. The authored look: full resolution, soft shadows and bloom. Changing this rebuilds the world.

items.label: GPU
items.note: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti/PCIe/SSE2. WebGL 2 is drawing on this GPU. On a dual-GPU laptop that should be the discrete chip, because the session asked for high-performance. Nothing is uploaded.

items.label: Menu size
items.note: Larger type and rows in every menu. The flight HUD keeps its size.

items.label: Render scale
items.note: Fewer pixels, then stretched to fit. The one lever that always helps a starved GPU, at the price of sharpness. 100 is native for the preset.

items.label: Performance mode
items.note: How the game holds its frame rate when the GPU falls behind. Balanced lowers the resolution a little while a scene is heavy and gives it back when it is not, with a light sharpen so it reads the same. Quality never lowers it. Performance lowers it sooner and further. Shadows and effects never change.

items.label: Frame cap
items.note: Caps how often the world is drawn. A steady 60 reads better than a heaving 90, and it spares the battery. Sticks are still read and the physics still steps every frame; only the picture waits.

items.label: Frame readout
items.note: A small box low on the left with the frame rate, the slowest 1 percent of frames, how long a frame takes and what it draws. F3 shows and hides it anywhere.

items.label: Mission guidance
items.note: In an ops mission, one objective line with its count, a ring on the objective and a chevron at the edge toward it. Off leaves the mission's voice and its briefs as they are.

items.label: HUD style
items.note: What the first person view draws over the picture. FPV OSD is the flight controller's own on screen display, the white characters it puts in the pilot's goggles: pack, current, timers, horizon, and the lap clock in the same type. Game is this game's own readout. Avionics is a sensor and tracking display: heading, speed and height tapes, the link, navigation and energy panels, the camera and the AI's tracks; H switches AI tracking, J the camera mode, K the zoom, I puts the camera full screen (J then picks thermal) and back, U sizes the camera inset, Y draws more or less (full, standard, minimal), . (period) changes the thermal palette. Each aircraft keeps its own choice, and the combat drones start on Avionics. Chase and line of sight always use the game's.

items.label: Pilot markers
items.note: In a room, a small mark in each pilot's colour shows where the others are when their aircraft is far away, hidden behind a hill or out of the picture: over the aircraft, or an arrow at the edge of the screen pointing the way. A pilot who is close and clear gets only their name. Minimal draws the marks without the names and ranges.

items.label: Thermal palette
items.note: How the thermal camera in white hot colours its picture: white hot, ironbow, rainbow or arctic (cold blue, hot orange), as a real camera offers them. Black hot stays its own camera mode (J). The . (period) key changes it in flight.

items.label: Sound
items.note: All sound: motors, wind, music and cues.

items.label: Radio subtitles
items.note: Crest Control's lines as one line captions in the war and the ops missions, with the sound on or off. The films keep their own.

items.label: Volume
items.note: Overall level. Zero to ten.

items.label: Motors and engines
items.note: The blade pass tone. You fly on its pitch, so keep some of it.

items.label: Wind
items.note: Air over the airframe. Rises with speed.

items.label: Other aircraft
items.note: Other pilots, attackers and vehicles.

items.label: Effects
items.note: Impacts, wrecks, explosions and the combat sounds.

items.label: Ambience
items.note: The world around you: wildlife, water, traffic.

items.label: Voice
items.note: The war radio's calls.

items.label: Music
items.note: Recorded tracks in flight, and a quieter bed in the menus. One level for both. The skip buttons on screen jump a track.

items.label: Music track
items.note: What flies. A random start, then every track in turn.

items.label: Binaural tone
items.note: A quiet 1000 Hz tone, 6 Hz apart between the ears. Needs headphones to do anything at all.

items.label: Weather
items.note: Still air, the same flight as always. In a room, the host's choice is everyone's.

items.label: Time of day
items.note: Each world at its own time, as always. In a room, the host's choice is everyone's; a mission keeps its own time.

items.label: Stock surfaces only
items.note: In a room you host: every pilot flies the control surfaces the plane came with, whatever tiers they have fitted. Each pilot's next run flies it.

items.label: Flight log
items.note: Record the run for download as a blackbox CSV. Holds the whole flight in memory.

items.label: Download flight log
items.note: Writes what was recorded as blackbox_decode CSV, which scripts/replay-log.js reads.

items.label: Download control recording
items.note: Every 1 ms step of the last minute: sticks, control surfaces, attitude and frame timing. Open it at /dev/hover.html.

items.label: Build
items.note: The version of the game this page runs. A bug report carries it.

items.label: Reset settings
items.note: Every setting back to its default. Your progress, paint, parts and stick calibration stay.

items.label: Reset progress
items.note: XP, challenges, medals, the campaign, flight time and best laps back to a new pilot's. Your settings stay.

items.label: Credits
items.note: Who made this, who flew it, and whose work it stands on.

items.label: Aircraft
items.note: An 880 gram stretched X 7 inch speed build on a 6S LiPo and 9 inch pitch two blades: the fastest quad here, built to run a strike drone down and ram it. Half a minute of full throttle in the pack. Changing it loads that machine's tune, its pack and its camera, and moves the track builder to the field that machine flies. Your own rates are kept unless they are still the stock ones.

items.label: Tune
items.note: Factory 4.5.1 on the interceptor: 1500 kV, an 1800 mAh LiPo. Opens PIDs, where the tune is chosen and the firmware's own sliders adjust it. Your rates are kept.

items.label: Firmware bench
items.note: Every firmware 4.5.1 key the module compiles, tab by tab, in the classic configurator colours. Opens as a tool, in its own frame. Save becomes Your edits and the Tune row above starts naming it; the picker that puts you back on stock is in PIDs. There is no CLI paste.

items.label: Camera angle
items.note: How far the camera tilts up from the airframe. 0 is flat, looking along the nose. 30 is a typical cruise. 45 to 55 is race. Above about 30, yaw starts to roll the horizon: at 45 degrees, 71 percent of a yaw shows up as roll in the picture. That is what a real tilted camera does. Lower Yaw max rate on the Rates screen to tame it.

items.label: Field of view
items.note: Wider sees more, narrower magnifies. 75 matches what an FPV lens does to the middle of the frame; 85 gives some of that back for width; 115 is the widest this projection can honestly offer, about 145 degrees corner to corner, and the gates will look smaller for it.

items.label: Camera shake
items.note: The picture's vibration, a hit's kick and a blast's buzz. Reduced or off for motion sickness; the aircraft flies the same.

items.label: Chase smoothing
items.note: How far the chase camera lags behind the aircraft. Smooth swings less in hard turns.

items.label: Flight mode
items.note: Acro: sticks are rates, hands off holds attitude. Angle: sticks are tilt, hands off levels. Racing on a keyboard always uses Angle. Freestyle uses this setting whatever you fly with, because Angle holds the craft to about thirty degrees of bank and no trick in the book can be flown in it.

items.label: Launch control
items.note: Launch control, off by default. When on, press L on the start line, pitch forward, centre the stick, then punch throttle. The quad holds the angle until you go.

items.label: Rates
items.note: Not the machine's. Rates are yours, so they live under Controller and stay put when you switch tunes. Each kind of aircraft keeps its own: a multirotor's, a plane's, a flying wing's and a glider's. This row goes there, and changing them mid run leaves the quad where it is.

items.note: Opens where the tune is chosen and its sliders adjust it. Changing the tune puts the quad back on the start line.

items.label: Rates
items.note: How far the sticks go, and the throttle limit. Yours, not the tune's: changing them leaves the quad where it is.

items.label: Flight feel
items.note: Tell the people tuning it how it flies. One word is enough; your aircraft, mode and rates go with it.

items.label: Quad setup
items.note: Camera, flight mode and the firmware bench. Back returns to the pause menu.

items.label: Customise
items.note: The power and the paint of the quad you are flying. Save puts them on it where it is.

items.label: HUD style
items.note: What the first person view draws over the picture. FPV OSD is the flight controller's own on screen display, the white characters it puts in the pilot's goggles: pack, current, timers, horizon, and the lap clock in the same type. Game is this game's own readout. items.label: Graphics
items.note: A 2021-era PC or a strong laptop. The authored look: full resolution, soft shadows and bloom. Changing this rebuilds the world.

items.label: Stick path
items.note: A key is not a stick. Holding one ramps the stick to 34 percent and stays there until about three quarters of a second, then stretches to full at one and a quarter. So the rates below are the rates a RADIO would fly: a tap reaches roughly a third of them, which is why keyboard flight feels firmer and slower to bite than the numbers say. A gamepad or a radio in USB joystick mode gets the whole curve.

items.label: Preset
items.note: Save the numbers below under a name and they come back in one press, which is what a second track wants. Presets are saved in this browser on this device only. Clearing site data, a private window, another browser or another device all start you from nothing, and there is no account and nothing is uploaded.

items.label: Rates type
items.note: Which rate system the numbers below are in. All five are the firmware's own and all five fly: the curve is chosen in fc/rc.c by this one field. Actual is the firmware 4.5 default and the one whose Max rate column means exactly what it says at the stop. Changing this loads that system's own defaults, because a Classic RC rate of 1.00 and an Actual centre sensitivity of 70 are the same stored number and not the same setting.

items.label: Separate pitch
items.note: Off. Roll and pitch share one set of numbers, which is how most quads are set up and what the firmware ships. Turn it on to give pitch its own.

items.label: Centre sensitivity
items.note: How quickly the quad answers a small stick move, as the SLOPE of the curve at the middle. Low is calm for a smooth line, high is twitchy and quick. It is not the rate at half stick: read the curve. Configurator apps call this column Center Sensitivity. At full stick this axis is 670 deg/s.

spec.label: Centre sensitivity
spec.note: How quickly the quad answers a small stick move, as the SLOPE of the curve at the middle. Low is calm for a smooth line, high is twitchy and quick. It is not the rate at half stick: read the curve. Configurator apps call this column Center Sensitivity.

items.label: Max rate
items.note: What the quad does at full stick, exactly. This is the number Actual rates exist for: the end of the curve is the number you type, whatever expo does to the middle. At full stick this axis is 670 deg/s.

spec.label: Max rate
spec.note: What the quad does at full stick, exactly. This is the number Actual rates exist for: the end of the curve is the number you type, whatever expo does to the middle.

items.label: Expo
items.note: How much of the travel is spent near the middle. Zero is a straight line from centre sensitivity to the stop. Higher softens the middle and keeps the same maximum, which is why the ends of the curve do not move when you change it.

spec.label: Centre sensitivity

items.label: Max rate
items.note: What the quad does at full stick, exactly. This is the number Actual rates exist for: the end of the curve is the number you type, whatever expo does to the middle. At full stick this axis is 670 deg/s. Quads yaw slower than they roll, so many pilots set yaw below roll. Your camera is tilted up 45 degrees, so 71 percent of a yaw rolls the horizon rather than turning it: 474 deg/s of picture roll at full pedal.

spec.note: What the quad does at full stick, exactly. This is the number Actual rates exist for: the end of the curve is the number you type, whatever expo does to the middle.

items.label: Throttle limit
items.note: Off. This quad is almost nine to one thrust to weight and hovers at 24.1 percent of stick, so most of the travel is above hover. Capping it scales the whole stick down and gives the resolution back.

items.label: Throttle mid
items.note: Where the curve pivots. 0.50 is the factory middle; pilots who hover low often bring it down toward their hover stick so the expo softens the right part of the travel. This quad hovers near 24.1 percent of stick on the factory curve.

spec.label: Throttle mid
spec.note: Where the curve pivots. 0.50 is the factory middle; pilots who hover low often bring it down toward their hover stick so the expo softens the right part of the travel.

items.label: Throttle expo
items.note: Flattens the throttle around the mid point and steepens the ends, exactly the firmware's thr_expo. 0 is the factory straight line.

spec.label: Throttle expo
spec.note: Flattens the throttle around the mid point and steepens the ends, exactly the firmware's thr_expo. 0 is the factory straight line.

items.label: Save as preset
items.note: Name these numbers and they come back in one press. Presets are saved in this browser on this device only. Clearing site data, a private window, another browser or another device all start you from nothing, and there is no account and nothing is uploaded.

items.label: Delete preset
items.note: Load a preset first. This deletes the profile the rows below are flying, and they are not flying a saved one.

items.label: Revert to defaults
items.note: Already on the firmware 4.5.1 defaults.

items.label: Flight feel
items.note: Tell the tune work how the quad flies. One word is enough; your tune, PID adjustment and rates go with it.

items.label: Room name
items.note: Enter to type a name, or leave it and the room gets a picked one, like the pilots' names.

items.label: Who joins
items.note: Solo: nobody. Friends: whoever you read the invite code to. Public: listed, anybody drops in.

items.label: The world
items.note: The world the room flies in.

items.label: Game
items.note: What the room is for. You are its host, and start the game from the room screen whenever you like.

items.label: Make the room
items.note: Makes it and puts you in it. It shows up in Rooms for everybody.

items.label: Make a room
items.note: Name it, choose who joins, the world and a game.

items.label: Join with a code
items.note: Type the six letter code a friend gave you.
